name: יְהוּכַל
summary: Jehucal son of Shelemiah, one of king Zedekiah's princes: sent with Zephaniah the priest to ask Jeremiah to pray to Yahweh for the city (Jer 37:3), and, as Jucal (יוּכַל), one of the princes who heard Jeremiah's words and asked the king to put him to death (Jer 38:1–4). The name is יְהוּ with the imperfect of יָכֹל, “Yahweh is able”; the shorter spelling יוּכַל is the bare verb form “he is able”, as in 2Ch 32:14. Scripture does not explain it.

evidence.note: Zedekiah sent “יְהוּכַל son of Shelemiah” to Jeremiah: “Pray now to Yahweh our God for us.”
“וְיוּכַל son of Shelemiahu” heard what Jeremiah spoke to all the people.
The princes said to the king, “Let this man be put to death.”
“That your God should be able (יוּכַל) to deliver you”: the verb form of the short spelling, in the question the name answers.
“Our God whom we serve is able to deliver us.”

note: Takes e.az.ap (יְהוּכַל) and e.az.bp (יוּכַל), which BDB files under הוה, with the cross-references j.bm.ab and j.ax.ai. TIPNR records both spellings under Jehucal@Jer.37.3. Jucal at Jer 38:1 is spelled as the verb's imperfect יוּכַל; check that the token is not also counted under the verb.
